targets.authors: Payne, B. K., Burkley, M. A., & Stokes, M. B.
targets.title: Why do implicit and explicit attitude tests diverge? The role of structural fit.
targets.evidence_quote:
Participants in the United States and Italy completed a procedure which aimed to directly
replicate Payne, Burkley, and Stokes (2008), Study 4.
targets.outcome_quote:
Regardless, while the current study did not replicate
the prior social pressure effect on implicit-explicit attitude relations, the overall pattern of
relations did support the structural fit hypothesis put forth by Payne, Burkley, and Stokes (2008),
with structurally similar attitude measures producing strong implicit-explicit correlations
regardless of sample source.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors state the focal social-pressure effect did not replicate, with reversal in the US and no reliable effect in Italy. Supporting the broader structural-fit hypothesis is not a successful replication of the focal effect.

reasoning: Eight sites retest one original paper. The authors explicitly identify Payne et al. Study 4 as their direct replication target; Vianello (2015) supplies an earlier attempt, materials and motivation for country moderation, not a separately stated retest target. The results-included project manuscript is completed full text, not the results-blind protocol. Original DOI is not printed.
